rules.title: Security Deposit Cap: One Month's Rent (General Rule)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security in an amount exceeding one month's rent, in addition to rent for the first month paid at or before occupancy.
rules.quotedSpan: Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month's rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.

rules.title: Security Deposit Cap: Six Months' Rent for Longer Leases
rules.requirement: A landlord may accept an advance payment of not less than six months' rent when the lease term is six months or longer, without this counting against the one-month security deposit cap.
rules.keyValue: 6 months' rent for leases of 6+ months
rules.quotedSpan: This subdivision does not prohibit an advance payment of not less than six months' rent if the term of the lease is six months or longer.
rules.coverageDescription: All residential rental properties with leases of six months or longer.

rules.title: Security Deposit Cap: Two Months' Rent for Small Owner-Operators
rules.effectiveDateQuote: This subdivision shall not apply to a security collected or demanded by the landlord before July 1, 2024.
rules.requirement: A natural person or LLC (whose members are all natural persons) owning no more than two residential rental properties with four or fewer total dwelling units may demand up to two months' rent in security (plus first month's rent), except for service members, who must follow the one-month cap.
rules.quotedSpan: Notwithstanding paragraph (1), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to two months' rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy if the landlord meets both of the following requirements: (i) The landlord is a natural person or a limited liability company in which all members are natural persons. (ii) The landlord owns no more than two residential rental properties that collectively include no more than four dwelling units offered for rent.
rules.coverageDescription: Owner-occupied or small-owner properties with no more than 4 dwelling units.
exemptions: This exemption does not apply to service members.
warnings: The rule assumes LLC means all members are natural persons; the text states this qualification.

rules.title: Higher Security Deposit for Service Members: Disclosure and Return Requirements
rules.effectiveDateQuote: On or after April 1, 2025, if a landlord or its agent charges a service member who rents residential property in which the service member will reside a higher than standard or advertised security pursuant to paragraph (1) due to the credit history, credit score, housing history, or other factor related to the tenant, the landlord shall provide the tenant with a written statement
rules.requirement: If a landlord charges a service member a security deposit higher than the standard amount due to credit history, credit score, housing history, or other tenant-related factors, the landlord must provide written explanation before lease signing and must return the excess amount after six months if the tenant is not in arrears.
rules.quotedSpan: On or after April 1, 2025, if a landlord or its agent charges a service member who rents residential property in which the service member will reside a higher than standard or advertised security pursuant to paragraph (1) due to the credit history, credit score, housing history, or other factor related to the tenant, the landlord shall provide the tenant with a written statement, on or before the date the lease is signed, of the amount of the higher security and an explanation why the higher security amount is being charged. The additional amount of security shall be returned to the tenant after no more than six months of residency if the tenant is not in arrears for any rent due during that period.
rules.coverageDescription: All residential rental properties where a service member is the tenant.
warnings: This rule applies only to service members as defined in Military and Veterans Code § 400.

rules.title: Security Deposit Uses
rules.requirement: A landlord may use security only for: tenant default in rent payment; repair of damages (beyond ordinary wear and tear) caused by the tenant or tenant's guests; cleaning necessary to return the unit to its inception condition; and remedying tenant defaults on rental agreement obligations (if authorized in the agreement).
rules.quotedSpan: 'security' means any payment, fee, deposit, or charge, including, but not limited to, any payment, fee, deposit, or charge, except as provided in Section 1950.6, that is imposed at the beginning of the tenancy to be used to reimburse the landlord for costs associated with processing a new tenant or that is imposed as an advance payment of rent, used or to be used for any purpose, including, but not limited to, any of the following: (1) The compensation of a landlord for a tenant's default in the payment of rent. (2) The repair of damages to the premises, exclusive of ordinary wear and tear, caused by the tenant or by a guest or licensee of the tenant.

rules.title: Exclusion of Ordinary Wear and Tear from Deductions
rules.requirement: A landlord may not deduct from security for preexisting damages, ordinary wear and tear, or cumulative wear-and-tear effects from any tenancy. Repairs must restore the unit to its inception condition, excluding ordinary wear and tear.
rules.quotedSpan: The landlord shall not assert a claim against the tenant or the security for damages to the premises or any defective conditions that preexisted the tenancy, for ordinary wear and tear or the effects thereof, whether the wear and tear preexisted the tenancy or occurred during the tenancy, or for the cumulative effects of ordinary wear and tear occurring during any one or more tenancies.

rules.title: Professional Cleaning and Material Cost Limits
rules.requirement: A landlord may not require a tenant to pay for or claim against security for professional cleaning unless reasonably necessary. Claims for repairs and materials must be limited to a reasonable amount necessary to restore the premises to its inception condition, excluding ordinary wear and tear.
rules.quotedSpan: Claims against the tenant or the security for materials or supplies and for work performed by a contractor, the landlord, or the landlord's employee shall be limited to a reasonable amount necessary to restore the premises back to the condition it was in at the inception of the tenancy, exclusive of ordinary wear and tear. (C) The landlord shall not require a tenant to pay for, or assert a claim against the tenant or the security for, professional carpet cleaning or other professional cleaning services, unless reasonably necessary to return the premises to the condition it was in at the inception of tenancy, exclusive of ordinary wear and tear.

rules.title: Initial Inspection Notification and Right to Request Inspection
rules.requirement: Within a reasonable time after notification of tenancy termination, a landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the right to request an initial inspection at least two weeks before the move-out date. The tenant may attend the inspection and remedy deficiencies to avoid security deductions.
rules.quotedSpan: Within a reasonable time after notification of either party's intention to terminate the tenancy, or before the end of the lease term, the landlord shall notify the tenant in writing of the tenant's option to request an initial inspection and of the tenant's right to be present at the inspection. At a reasonable time, but no earlier than two weeks before the termination or the end of lease date, the landlord, or an agent of the landlord, shall, upon the request of the tenant, make an initial inspection of the premises prior to any final inspection the landlord makes after the tenant has vacated the premises.
exemptions: The requirements do not apply when the tenancy is terminated pursuant to Cal. Code Civ. Proc. § 1161(2)–(4) (unlawful detainer proceedings).

rules.title: Itemized Statement After Initial Inspection
rules.requirement: After an initial inspection, the landlord must provide an itemized statement describing proposed repairs or cleanings and the statutory basis for deductions, and the tenant has an opportunity to remedy deficiencies before move-out.
rules.quotedSpan: Based on the inspection, the landlord shall give the tenant an itemized statement specifying repairs or cleanings that are proposed to be the basis of any deductions from the security the landlord intends to make pursuant to paragraphs (1) to (4), inclusive, of subdivision (b). This statement shall also include the texts of paragraphs (1) to (4), inclusive, of subdivision (b).
rules.coverageDescription: All residential rental properties where an initial inspection was requested.

rules.title: Limitation on Deductions Without Initial Inspection
rules.requirement: If an initial inspection is conducted and the premises are not blocked by tenant possessions, the landlord may not deduct for repairs or cleanings not identified in the initial inspection statement, except for damages between inspection and return of possession or those that could not be seen due to possessions.
rules.quotedSpan: if an initial inspection is conducted pursuant to this subdivision and, at the time of inspection, the premises do not contain tenant possessions that prevent the landlord from identifying repairs or cleanings due to the presence of those possessions, the landlord shall not use the security for deductions for repairs or cleanings that are not identified in the itemized statement described in paragraph (2).
rules.coverageDescription: All residential rental properties where an initial inspection was conducted.

rules.title: Photography Documentation Requirements (Inception and Return)
rules.effectiveDateQuote: For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit immediately before, or at the inception of, the tenancy. Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after the possession of the unit is returned to the landlord
rules.requirement: For tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025, a landlord must photograph the unit at inception and within a reasonable time after the tenant vacates but before any repairs or cleanings, and again after repairs/cleanings are completed. Beginning April 1, 2025, return documentation applies to all tenancies.
rules.quotedSpan: For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit immediately before, or at the inception of, the tenancy. Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after the possession of the unit is returned to the landlord, but prior to any repairs or cleanings for which the landlord will make a deduction from or claim against the security deposit pursuant to this section, and shall also take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after such repairs or cleanings are completed.
warnings: Different effective dates apply: July 1, 2025 for inception photos (new tenancies); April 1, 2025 for return/post-repair photos (all tenancies).

rules.title: Security Deposit Return Deadline and Itemized Statement
rules.requirement: No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates (but not earlier than when either party gives termination notice or 60 days before lease expiration), the landlord must return any remaining security with an itemized statement indicating the basis and amount of any deductions.
rules.quotedSpan: No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated the premises, but not earlier than the time that either the landlord or the tenant provides a notice to terminate the tenancy under Section 1946 or 1946.1, Section 1161 of the Code of Civil Procedure, or not earlier than 60 calendar days prior to the expiration of a fixed-term lease, the landlord shall furnish the tenant, a copy of an itemized statement indicating the basis for, and the amount of, any security received and the disposition of the security, and shall return any remaining portion of the security to the tenant

rules.title: Method of Return of Security Deposit (Default and Alternative Methods)
rules.requirement: The landlord must return security by personal delivery or first-class mail check. If the landlord received rent electronically, the tenant may request electronic return. Multiple adult tenants share a check by default unless they mutually agree otherwise. The tenant may designate a different address or agree to email delivery of the itemized statement.
rules.quotedSpan: the landlord shall return the remainder of the security by personal delivery or by a check made payable to the tenant and mailed by first-class mail, postage prepaid. (ii) (I) If the landlord received the security or rental payments from the tenant electronically, the landlord shall return the remainder of the security electronically to a bank account or other financial institution designated by the tenant in writing, or by any electronic or virtual method available to the landlord if agreed to in writing by the tenant.

rules.title: Documentation of Deductions (Contractor Bills and Photos)
rules.effectiveDateQuote: Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after the possession of the unit is returned to the landlord, but prior to any repairs or cleanings for which the landlord will make a deduction from or claim against the security deposit pursuant to this section, and shall also take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after such repairs or cleanings are completed.
rules.requirement: The landlord must include copies of bills, invoices, receipts from contractors or vendors, or reasonably describe work done by the landlord/employee (with time and hourly rate), and provide photographs and a written explanation of costs. Estimates are allowed if work cannot be completed within 21 days.
rules.quotedSpan: The landlord shall also include, along with and at the same time the itemized statement is sent, copies of documents showing charges incurred and deducted by the landlord to repair or clean the premises, as follows: (A) If the landlord or landlord's employee did the work, the itemized statement shall reasonably describe the work performed. The itemized statement shall include the time spent and the reasonable hourly rate charged. (B) If the landlord or landlord's employee did not do the work, the landlord shall provide the tenant a copy of the bill, invoice, or receipt supplied by the person or entity performing the work.
rules.coverageDescription: All residential rental properties where deductions are claimed.
exemptions: Landlord need not comply if deductions total $125 or less, or if the tenant waived these rights in writing (after termination notice was given).
warnings: Documentation requirement applies beginning April 1, 2025 for photography; older provisions apply to bills/invoices.

rules.title: Tenant Request for Documentation
rules.requirement: Notwithstanding the $125 deduction threshold or waiver, if a tenant requests documentation within 14 calendar days after receiving the itemized statement, the landlord must comply within 14 calendar days of receiving the request.
rules.quotedSpan: Notwithstanding paragraph (4), the landlord shall comply with paragraphs (2) and (3) when a tenant makes a request for documentation within 14 calendar days after receiving the itemized statement specified in paragraph (1). The landlord shall comply within 14 calendar days after receiving the request from the tenant.

rules.title: Bad Faith Claim: Statutory Damages
rules.requirement: A landlord's bad faith claim, retention, or demand for replacement of security in violation of this section may subject the landlord to statutory damages up to twice the amount of the security, plus actual damages. The court may award damages regardless of whether the tenant requested it.
rules.quotedSpan: The bad faith claim or retention by a landlord or the landlord's successors in interest of the security or any portion thereof in violation of this section, or the bad faith demand of replacement of security in violation of subdivision (k), may subject the landlord or the landlord's successors in interest to statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages.

rules.title: Nonrefundable Fee Prohibition
rules.requirement: A lease or rental agreement may not characterize any security as 'nonrefundable.'
rules.quotedSpan: A lease or rental agreement shall not contain a provision characterizing any security as "nonrefundable."

rules.title: Transfer of Security to Successor in Interest
rules.requirement: Upon termination of the landlord's interest in the property (by sale, assignment, death, or otherwise), the landlord or agent must either transfer the security to the successor in interest with written notice to the tenant or return it to the tenant with an accounting. The successor is jointly and severally liable if the transfer or notice is not made.
rules.quotedSpan: Upon termination of the landlord's interest in the premises, whether by sale, assignment, death, appointment of receiver, or otherwise, the landlord or the landlord's agent shall, within a reasonable time, do one of the following acts, either of which shall relieve the landlord of further liability with respect to the security held: (1) Transfer the portion of the security remaining after any lawful deductions are made under subdivision (e) to the landlord's successor in interest.

rules.title: Small Claims Court Jurisdiction
rules.requirement: An action under this section may be maintained in small claims court if the damages claimed (actual, statutory, or both) are within the jurisdictional amount allowed by California Code of Civil Procedure sections 116.220 or 116.221.
rules.quotedSpan: An action under this section may be maintained in small claims court if the damages claimed, whether actual, statutory, or both, are within the jurisdictional amount allowed by Section 116.220 or 116.221 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

warnings: The statute applies to 'residential property that is used as the dwelling of the tenant' (§1950.5(a)). The rules above assume all properties in the dataset are residential rentals.

The rule on higher security for small owner-operators (two-month cap, §1950.5(c)(5)) applies only if the landlord is a natural person or LLC where all members are natural persons. The text defines 'natural person' to include beneficiaries of family trusts.
Service member status is defined under California Military and Veterans Code § 400, which is not included in this source.
Amended effective January 1, 2026 by Stats. 2025, Ch. 340, Sec. 1 (AB 414). Several provisions have dates between 2025 and 2026 that may not be fully in force until then.
The statute permits advance rent of six months or more under §1950.5(c)(2), but this is treated as advance rent, not security; it does not count against the one-month security cap.
